pages.text: As water is driven off, the brine concentrates by 1/(1 − f). Each salt comes out when its solubility product is passed: gypsum at about four times, halite at ten to twenty, and the bittern - rich in lithium - at thirty and beyond. Heat drives the water off faster (it follows the vapour pressure), but crystals that grow too fast trap the other salts.
$(thing)Set$(): Pan temperature, Water driven off.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Wind and sun: the evaporation rate varies by ±3%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): none beyond the recipe windows.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): The faster the water goes, the faster the salt comes.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Concentration factor: CF = 1/(1 − f)$(br)Evaporation rate: v ∝ e^(−L/R·(1/T − 1/330 K))$(br)Crystal purity: purity = e^(−(v − 1))
